pull.title: musig: Clear secrets before ARG_CHECK failures in partial_sign
pull.body:
`secp256k1_musig_partial_sign` loads the two secret nonce scalars and then zeroes the secnonce, so the stack copies are the only ones left. The `ARG_CHECK`s that follow, four on NULL arguments and one on the secnonce matching the keypair, return without calling `secp256k1_musig_partial_sign_clear`, which every other exit after the load calls.

This clears the secrets before each of these checks fails, as #1849 did for `secp256k1_musig_nonce_gen_counter`. The checks keep their order, and the secnonce is still zeroed when the call fails; a new test checks that. It matters only when the illegal callback returns and the API is misused, the key mismatch being the realistic case.

events.body: Tested ACK edeb2376e19013e752629505ba695a57a7490732 on Windows x86_64.
Concept ACK on clearing the secret, but I think this could be simplified by loading the secnonce only after the ARG_CHECKS

Thanks @real-or-random, done in 986d6ad (force-pushed): the NULL checks now come before the secnonce is loaded, so a call with a NULL argument leaves the secnonce as is and produces no signature. The key-match check needs both the secnonce and the keypair loaded, so it still clears the secrets before it fails. The header says the function "overwrites the given secnonce with zeros"; should it note the NULL case?

@Yudis-bit, the head changed: could you re-test 986d6ad and renew your ACK if it still holds?

Tested ACK 986d6ad on Windows x86_64.

I don't think the header needs to mention the NULL case either, passing NULL is already invalid API usage under ARG_NONNULL.

> the NULL checks now come before the secnonce is loaded, so a call with a NULL argument leaves the secnonce as is and produces no signature.

Now that I see your comment, I'm pretty sure that my suggestion was simply misguided. Clearing the secnonce was deliberate, even if we fail, so we should keep this. Sorry.

musig: Clear secrets before ARG_CHECK failures in partial_sign

secp256k1_musig_partial_sign loads the secnonce scalars into stack
variables and zeroes the secnonce, so those copies are the only ones
left. The ARG_CHECKs after that point return without calling
secp256k1_musig_partial_sign_clear, which leaves the secrets on the
stack. Clear them before these checks fail.

Also test that the secnonce is zeroed when signing fails.

events.body:
Restored in 379a2f0: the secnonce is again zeroed before the NULL checks, as on master, and the secrets are cleared before any of the later `ARG_CHECK`s fails. A new test checks that the secnonce is zeroed when the call fails on a NULL argument; it fails on the previous head.

@theStack, the key match is now computed once into `secnonce_matches_keypair`, which the `if` and the `ARG_CHECK` both use. I also rebased on master.

comments.body: to avoid doing these comparisons twice, we could store the result in a variable (e.g. `secnonce_matches_keypair`) and then branch and `ARG_CHECK` on that
